title: Engineering Ops Constraints - Polaris Rollout

blocks.text: Engineering Operations Hard Limits
Monitoring Capacity
The SRE team can monitor a maximum of 4 concurrent rollout waves across all features. Each distinct customer segment (tier/region/percentage bracket) in an active rollout counts as one wave.
Customer Tier SLA Separation Rules
Enterprise tier customers CANNOT be in the same rollout wave as Starter tier customers (SLA guarantee conflict)
Professional tier can be grouped with either Enterprise OR Starter, but mixing all three tiers in one wave is prohibited
Mid-market accounts (subset of Professional tier) require dedicated monitoring and cannot share waves with Starter tier
Rollout Configuration Limits

Engineering can support up to 3 different rollout strategies running in parallel (e.g., one feature rolling by tier, another by region, another by percentage). Exceeding this creates unmanageable operational complexity.
Rollback Capability
Fast rollback (< 15 minutes) is only guaranteed for waves affecting fewer than 150 customers. Waves with 150+ customers require 45-90 minute rollback windows.

Enterprise tier: 87 customers (high SLA, 24/7 support)
Professional tier: 243 customers (includes 38 mid-market accounts flagged for churn risk)
Starter tier: 412 customers (standard SLA)

title: SRE Capacity Constraints & Rollback Buffer Policy - Polaris v1

blocks.text: SRE Capacity Constraints - April 2026
This document defines SRE capacity constraints and rollback buffer requirements for Polaris v1 GA launch windows in April 2026.
1. On-Call Rotation Schedule
Week of April 14: Marcus Chen (primary), David Torres (secondary) - 12 SRE hours available
Week of April 21: Sarah Kim (primary - auth focus), Marcus Chen (secondary) - 16 SRE hours available, split coverage
Week of April 28: Marcus Chen (primary), Rachel Kim (secondary) - 20 SRE hours available, full coverage
2. Infrastructure Allocation by Window
Window A (Apr 14-15): 85% compute, 70% database pool, 80% CDN capacity
Window B (Apr 21-22): 90% compute, 80% database pool, 85% CDN capacity
Window C (Apr 28-29): 95% compute, 90% database pool, 95% CDN capacity
3. Rollback Buffer Policy
3.1 Policy Statement

All platform launches require a minimum 72-hour rollback readiness buffer before the next critical platform milestone or hard-gated event (e.g., auth migration checkpoints, leadership reviews, customer-facing feature releases).
3.2 Rationale

72-hour buffer ensures: (1) adequate time for rollback execution if launch issues are detected; (2) post-rollback validation and system stabilization; (3) incident retrospective and communication to stakeholders; (4) no resource contention with subsequent platform events.
3.3 Constraint Violations
Window A: Rollback buffer ends April 17 EOD. Q2 Leadership Review on April 15 creates PM availability conflict during critical launch window. Not a buffer violation but an availability constraint.

Window B: Rollback buffer ends April 24 EOD. Auth Migration Checkpoint 2 on April 23 = only 48-hour buffer. VIOLATES 72-hour policy. Additionally, SRE coverage split between Polaris and auth creates resource contention risk.
Window C: Rollback buffer ends May 1 EOD. Next platform milestone (monitoring review) on May 2 = 96-hour buffer. SATISFIES 72-hour policy with 24-hour margin.
4. Recommended Window
Window C (April 28-29) is the only window that satisfies all hard constraints: adequate SRE capacity, no calendar conflicts, 72+ hour rollback buffer, and optimal infrastructure allocation.

**Decision**: Allocate 40% of data pipeline capacity to Polaris analytics workload starting April 7, with automatic scaling trigger at 75% utilization.

title: Q2 2026 Platform API Rate Limit Allocation - Capacity Model & Customer Tiers

blocks.text: Q2 2026 Platform API Rate Limit Budget
Last updated: April 3, 2026 by Marcus Chen (SRE Lead)
Hard Capacity Constraints
Total platform API capacity: 300,000 calls/hour (peak burst)
Sustainable capacity (hard cap): 285,000 calls/hour
Safety buffer requirement: 15,000 calls/hour (5% minimum unallocated)
Current allocated (as of April 1): 267,500 calls/hour (93.9% utilization)
Available headroom: 17,500 calls/hour
Why This Is a Hard Cap
Exceeding 285K sustained calls/hour triggers cascading failures:
API gateway cluster: Sized for 300K peak with 15K burst buffer. Sustained load above 285K causes request queuing and timeout cascades.
Database connection pool: 2,400 connections at 88% steady-state utilization. Additional 5K calls/hour pushes pool to 94%, risking connection exhaustion.
SLA risk: Exceeding cap would cause P50 latency degradation for all customers, triggering SLA violation credits.
Current Allocation by Tier (April 1, 2026)
Per-Customer Allocations (Enterprise Tier)
Upcoming Capacity Releases
Polaris GA (April 28-30 window): Database query optimization and caching layer adds ~35,000 calls/hour capacity
Auth migration completion (May 15 target): Legacy endpoint retirement frees ~22,000 calls/hour
Total Q2 capacity additions: ~57,000 calls/hour (if both ship on time)
Allocation Policy
Any rate limit increase must satisfy ALL constraints:
Total allocated ≤ 285,000 - 14,250 = 270,750 calls/hour (maintains 5% buffer)
No single customer exceeds 20% of total capacity (57,000 calls/hour max)
Tier-based allocation ratios maintained (Enterprise 65-70%, Mid-Market 25-30%, Growth 5-8%)
Increases above 10K calls/hour require VP Engineering approval

title: Q2 2026 Platform Capacity Planning - Process Guide & Approval Thresholds

blocks.text: Q2 Platform Capacity Planning Process

This guide documents the end-to-end capacity planning process for Q2 2026, including infrastructure constraint modeling, rate limit allocation policies, SRE capacity coordination, and OKR dependency management.
Step 1: Infrastructure Constraint Assessment

Review current infrastructure utilization across compute, database, and CDN resources. Reference NPAG-24 for detailed infrastructure requirements and dependency mapping. Key metrics: compute quota utilization (target <75%), DB connection pool allocation (max 2000 connections), CDN bandwidth allocation by tier.
Step 2: Rate Limit Allocation Model

Apply tier-based rate limit allocation per NPAG-9. Enterprise tier: 10,000 req/min baseline, Mid-Market: 2,500 req/min, Startup: 500 req/min. Burst allowance: 150% of baseline for 5-minute windows. Cross-reference customer escalation history (NPAG-8) to identify accounts requiring custom allocation.
Step 3: SRE Capacity Policy & Rollback Buffer

Per NPAG-7, maintain 20% SRE capacity buffer for incident response and rollback operations. No more than 3 major deployments per week. Rollback window requirement: 4-hour buffer between deployments to same service cluster. Coordinate with Marcus Chen (SRE lead) for capacity reservation.
Step 4: OKR Planning Dependencies

Map capacity requirements to Q2 OKRs. Reference NPAG-7 for cross-team dependencies. Data team pipeline capacity affects analytics feature rollout. Platform team migration work (auth endpoint deprecation) consumes 30% of sprint capacity through Q2. Identify conflicts early and escalate to VP Engineering.
Approval Thresholds

items: Compute quota increase >15%: VP Engineering approval required
DB connection pool expansion: DBA + SRE lead sign-off required
Custom rate limit allocation (>2x tier baseline): Customer Success VP + Platform PM approval
SRE capacity buffer reduction below 20%: CTO approval required
Cross-team OKR dependency changes: Affected team leads + VP Engineering alignment

blocks.text: Cross-Team Coordination Requirements

Weekly sync with Data team (Sarah Kim) on pipeline capacity. Bi-weekly checkpoint with Customer Success (Rachel Kim) on tier allocation impact. Monthly infrastructure review with SRE (Marcus Chen) and Ops (David Torres). Decision log all capacity policy exceptions in weekly platform team review.
Real-World Example: Polaris Rollout (Feb 2026)

See NPAG-10 for decision log. Polaris GA required mixing Enterprise and Mid-Market customers in wave 3 to avoid DB connection pool cap (1800/2000 limit). Exception approved by VP Engineering after constraint-satisfaction proof. Key lesson: Model resource contention early and enumerate rollout strategies by tier, region, and feature-flag percentage.

title: Platform Team Launch Policy - Minimum Constraints & SLAs

blocks.text: Platform Team Launch Policy - Minimum Constraints & SLAs
This document defines hard floor constraints for all platform GA launches. These constraints are non-negotiable unless escalated to VP Engineering for exception approval.
Hard Floor Constraints
Minimum rollback buffer: 16 hours before next scheduled deployment window or infrastructure maintenance window
Minimum customer notice period: 14 days for GA launches affecting API contracts or SLA commitments
Minimum SRE on-call coverage: 18 hours continuous coverage starting from launch time
CDN migration requirement: CDN optimization layer must be active within 48 hours of GA launch for enterprise-tier customers
Platform Team Priority Weights
When evaluating launch windows that satisfy hard floor constraints, apply the following priority ordering:
Launch reliability (rollback buffer duration, SRE coverage hours, incident response capacity)
Customer experience (communication lead time, CDN availability, business-hours impact)
Engineering convenience (weekend availability, deployment slot timing)
Exception Process
Any launch window violating hard floor constraints requires written exception approval from VP Engineering (Priya Sharma) with documented business justification and risk mitigation plan.
